editorial.bodyTr: An editorial on military tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and pressure for U.S. troop deployment: The Korean government is carefully reviewing whether to dispatch troops amid mounting military tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and pressure from the United States. As the government considers economic security, the Korea-U.S. alliance, international legal legitimacy, and national interests, it is crucial to proceed with transparent procedures and build public consensus.

editorial.body: 이재명 대통령이 임기 제한 준수를 언급하며 연임 개헌 논란 진화에 나섰음. 정치권의 소모적 공방을 멈추고 민생 등 국가 현안에 집중해야 한다는 목소리가 높음. 현실적으로 개헌 가능성이 희박한 상황에서 불필요한 논란을 종결할 필요성이 제기됨.

정치권은 소모적 공방을 멈추고 민생에 집중해야 한다.

editorial.titleTr: Editorial: Time to End the Debate Over a Unrealistic Term Limit Amendment
summaryTr: President Lee Jae-myung has moved to quell the controversy over constitutional revision for reelection.
The political sphere must cease wasteful confrontation and focus on people's livelihoods.
It is time to end the unrealistic constitutional revision debate once and for all.
editorial.bodyTr: President Lee Jae-myung has moved to ease the constitutional amendment controversy over consecutive terms by mentioning his adherence to term limits. Calls are mounting for the political arena to end wasteful partisan bickering and focus on urgent national issues including people's livelihoods. Given the slim prospects for constitutional revision in practical terms, there is a growing need to put an end to unnecessary disputes.

summaryTr: Democratic Party senior official proposes unconstitutional bill to circumvent expulsion of lawmakers
Party leader presumes Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon's trial as '99.9% guilty'
Critics point out inappropriate remarks lacking political prudence
editorials.bodyTr: Democratic Party floor leader Kim Min-seok has introduced a bill to extend the suspension of parliamentary attendance to one year and has called for the expulsion of a specific lawmaker. This has drawn criticism as an unconstitutional attempt to circumvent constitutional requirements for expulsion. Additionally, he has made inappropriate remarks unbecoming of a ruling party leader, such as declaring Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon's trial outcome as 99.9 percent guilty before a verdict. He is being evaluated as lacking political prudence in his conduct and statements.

editorial.body: 입력 용혜인 성평등가족부 장관 후보자가 10일 오후 국회 소통관에서 기자회견을 마친 뒤 물을 마시고 있다. 임현동 기자 성평등가족부 장관 후보자로 지명된 기본소득당 용혜인 의원이 어제 자신에게 쏟아지는 비판을 반박하며 장관과 국회의원직을 모두 유지하겠다는 입장을 밝혔다. 국회의원과 국무위원의 겸직은 법률로 허용된다며 지역구 의원과 달리 비례대표 의원만 장관이 되면 사퇴하는 관례는 정치인들 사이의 자리 나눠먹기가 아니냐는 반론을 폈다. 그러나 이는 대의 민주주의의 기본 원칙과 비례대표 제도의 본질을 왜곡한 궤변에 불과하다. 지역구 의원과 비례대표 의원은 대표성이 다르다. 지역구 의원은 해당 지역 유권자들이 인물과 공약 등을 보고 투표로 뽑는다. 지역구 의원이 장관직 수행 등의 이유로 사퇴하면 주민을 대변할 창구가 사라져 보궐선거를 치러야 한다. 반면에 비례대표 의원은 후보 개인이 아닌 정당이 얻은 득표율에 따라 의석을 배분한다. 정당의 정책과 가치, 공천 순번 등을 보고 투표하기 때문에 의원이 사퇴하더라도 다음 비례 순번이 승계하면 공백이 생기지 않는다. 용 후보자가 의원직 사퇴를 거부하는 것은 자신이 속한 기본소득당을 원내 정당으로 유지하려는 셈법에 지나지 않는다. 사퇴하면 비례대표 자리가 민주당 인사로 바뀌기 때문이다. 더 나아가 용 후보자는 자신의 후보자 지명이 야당 현역 의원을 장관으로 지명한 것이라고 표현했는데 이는 어불성설이다. 용 후보자는 현 야당 소속으로 출마해 당선된 것이 아니다. 2024년 민주당 위성정당인 더불어민주연합의 비례대표 후보로 당선된 뒤 ‘꼼수 제명’ 절차를 거쳐 기본소득당으로 돌아갔고, 그 덕분에 기본소득당은 원내 의석을 보유한 정당으로 분류돼 국고보조금을 받고 있는 것이다. 2020년 첫 당선도 똑같은 패턴이었다. 이런 내력을 천하가 다 아는데 야당 의원으로 지명됐다고 하니, 여야 협치의 모범 사례라도 된단 말인가. 더구나 그 관계를 ‘DJP(김대중·김종필) 연합’에 비유했으니 자신에 대한 과대평가가 도를 넘는다. 용 후보자는 왜 여권 내부에서도 의원직 사퇴 불가피론, 더 나아가 낙마 불가피론까지 나오는지 진지하게 생각해 보기 바란다. 공정의 가치가 중시되는 시대에 편법과 꼼수의 덕을 입은 정치인을 대한민국 장관의 적임자라 할 수 있는가.

editorial.titleTr: Editorial: How Can Candidate Yong Hye-in, Who Came From a Satellite Party, Be an Opposition Lawmaker?
summaryTr: Rep. Yong Hye-in of the Basic Income Party declares her intention to maintain dual positions as lawmaker after being nominated as minister of gender equality and family.
She argues that proportional representation seats are allocated based on a party's vote share, making resignation unnecessary as a matter of convention.
Editorial: The nomination of a politician elected through satellite party loopholes as minister contradicts principles of fairness.
editorial.bodyTr:
Rep. Yong Hye-in of the Basic Income Party, nominated as minister of gender equality and family, refuted criticism directed at her yesterday and stated that she would maintain both her ministerial post and her seat in the National Assembly. She argued that the concurrent holding of a parliamentary seat and cabinet position is permitted by law, and countered that the convention requiring proportional representation lawmakers—unlike district representatives—to resign upon becoming minister is nothing but politicians dividing up positions among themselves. However, this is merely sophistry that distorts the fundamental principles of representative democracy and the essence of the proportional representation system.

District representatives and proportional representation lawmakers have different representational mandates. District representatives are elected by voters in their constituencies who cast ballots based on individual candidates and their pledges. When a district representative resigns due to ministerial duties or other reasons, the constituency loses its representative voice and must hold a by-election. In contrast, proportional representation seats are allocated based on the vote share earned by the party, not individual candidates. Since voters decide based on party policy, values, and nomination order, when a proportional representative resigns, no vacancy occurs as the next person on the party list assumes the seat.

Rep. Yong's refusal to resign from her parliamentary seat is merely a calculation to maintain her Basic Income Party's status as a represented party in the legislature. If she resigns, her proportional seat would go to a Democratic Party member. Furthermore, Rep. Yong described her nomination as appointing an incumbent opposition legislator to minister, which is patently absurd. She was not elected as a candidate from the current opposition party. She was elected as a proportional representation candidate for the Democratic Party's satellite party, the Together Democratic Union, in 2024, then returned to the Basic Income Party through a "loophole removal" procedure, which enabled the Basic Income Party to be classified as a represented party and receive government subsidies. The same pattern occurred in her initial election in 2020. Everyone knows this history, yet she claims she was nominated as an opposition lawmaker—as if this exemplifies inter-party cooperation? Moreover, by comparing this relationship to the "DJP Alliance," her self-assessment has become utterly excessive.

Rep. Yong should seriously consider why even within the ruling bloc, calls for her to resign from her parliamentary seat—and even demands for her withdrawal—have emerged. In an era when the value of fairness is paramount, can a politician who has benefited from loopholes and procedural tricks be deemed a suitable candidate for minister of the Republic of Korea?

editorial.title: Paper prosperity
editorial.body: Korea nears $40,000 per capita GNI, but growth is uneven, youth struggle for jobs A nation can cross a $40,000 income threshold without a single dollar reaching the average kitchen table. That uncomfortable contradiction now captures the dilemma at the heart of South Korea’s economy. The Bank of Korea on Tuesday projected that per capita gross national income will exceed $40,000 in 2026, assuming exchange rates hold steady and external shocks stay at bay. After 12 years in the $30,000 range since first crossing that threshold in 2014, the country is finally poised to move up. The milestone is meaningful; however, it is an unusually poor measure of how evenly the economy generates and distributes new income. The latest national accounts explain why. Nominal gross domestic product jumped 26.4 percent from a year earlier in the second quarter, its fastest increase since 1979. Real GNI rose 15.6 percent, the strongest annual gain since 1988. Much of that acceleration, however, comes from a semiconductor boom fueled by global AI investment. In the first eight months, semiconductors accounted for 40.6 percent of exports, with shipments surging 169.6 percent from a year earlier. Such concentration matters because national income is an average. It can rise sharply even when the gains are concentrated in a narrow slice of the economy. The exchange rate adds another layer. Per capita GNI is expressed in dollars, so a stronger won can lift the figure even when productive capacity has changed little. The won’s movement from near 1,600 per dollar to the 1,300s has further inflated the dollar-denominated figure. More important is what happens after corporate profits rise. Chipmakers like Samsung Electronics and SK hynix can earn enormous sums without creating a comparable number of domestic jobs. Gross operating surplus, for instance, rose 18.5 percent in the second quarter from the previous quarter, while employee compensation increased just 1.9 percent. Some gains may reach households through wages, bonuses and dividends, but the path is neither immediate nor assured. Young workers have little reason to celebrate the headline figure. Employment among people aged 15 to 29 fell for the 46th consecutive month in August, declining by 143,000 from a year earlier. Among unemployed young people, 52.7 percent reported experiencing burnout, according to a government survey. Equally problematic is productivity. Korea has become exceptionally good at adding capital to its strongest industries, while productivity gains elsewhere remain modest. A savings rate of 45.6 percent in the second quarter shows that money is hardly scarce. The question is where it goes. Capital needs to flow toward research, new businesses and human capital. Labor markets and education also need to help workers move into areas where demand is growing. Yet workplace-based vocational training accounted for only 1.5 percent of Korea’s training expenditure in 2024, compared with an OECD average of 11.7 percent. The government should treat $40,000 as a checkpoint, not a trophy. Its priority should be raising productivity beyond semiconductors, expanding effective training and reducing the household debt burden that suppresses consumption. Fiscal policy should also avoid stimulating demand in ways that run against monetary restraint. Korea’s journey from a meager $67 in per capita income in 1953 to $40,000 is an undisputed triumph. Yet an economy that depends heavily on capital concentrated in a few industries and favorable valuation effects offers no guarantee of lasting stability. Unless structural reforms broaden the flow of corporate gains to households, raise productivity beyond the leading industries and reconnect young workers with the labor market, $40,000 will stand as a paper victory, reflecting a high-water mark on corporate balance sheets rather than broad-based prosperity. 국가가 4만 달러 소득 기준을 넘어도 그 돈이 평범한 가정의 식탁에 단 한 푼도 닿지 않을 수 있다. 이러한 불편한 모순은 이제 한국 경제의 핵심 딜레마를 대변하고 있다. 한국은행은 지난 화요일 환율이 현 수준을 유지하고 대외 충격이 없다면 2026년 1인당 국민총소득이 4만 달러를 초과할 것으로 전망했다. 2014년 처음 4만 달러 기준을 넘은 후 12년간 3만 달러 대에 머물렀던 한국이 이제 마침내 도약할 준비를 갖춘 것이다. 이 지표는 의미 있지만, 경제가 새로운 소득을 얼마나 고르게 창출하고 배분하는지를 나타내는 지표로서는 특이하게 부족하다. 최근 국민계정이 그 이유를 설명해준다. 명목 국내총생산이 2분기에 전년 동기 대비 26.4% 급증했으며, 이는 1979년 이후 가장 큰 증가율이다. 실질 국민총소득은 15.6% 올랐으며, 이는 1988년 이후 가장 강한 연간 증가율이다. 그러나 이러한 가속화의 상당 부분은 글로벌 인공지능 투자에 힘입은 반도체 호황에서 비롯되었다. 지난 8개월간 반도체가 수출의 40.6%를 차지했으며, 출하량이 전년 동기 대비 169.6% 급증했다. 이러한 집중도가 중요한 이유는 국민소득이 평균치이기 때문이다. 이익이 경제의 좁은 부분에 집중되어 있어도 국민소득은 급격히 상승할 수 있다. 환율이 또 다른 변수를 더한다. 1인당 국민총소득은 달러로 표시되므로, 강한 원화는 생산 능력이 크게 변하지 않았어도 이 수치를 높일 수 있다. 원화가 달러당 1,600원대에서 1,300원대로 움직인 것이 달러 기준 수치를 더욱 부풀렸다. 더 중요한 것은 기업 이익이 증가한 후 무슨 일이 일어나는가이다. 삼성전자, SK하이닉스 같은 반도체 제조업체들은 국내 일자리 창출과 비례하는 막대한 수익을 얻을 수 있다. 예를 들어, 2분기 영업잉여는 분기 대비 18.5% 증가했지만, 근로자 보상은 겨우 1.9% 증가했다. 일부 이익이 임금, 상여금, 배당금을 통해 가계에 도달할 수도 있지만, 그 경로는 즉각적이지도, 확실하지도 않다. 청년 노동자들이 이 통계상의 숫자를 축하할 이유는 거의 없다. 15~29세 인구의 취업자 수는 8월 46개월 연속 감소했으며, 전년 동기 대비 14만 3천 명이 줄었다. 실업 상태의 청년 중 52.7%가 정부 조사에서 소진을 경험했다고 보고했다. 똑같이 문제가 되는 것은 생산성이다. 한국은 가장 강한 산업에 자본을 추가하는 데는 탁월해졌으나, 다른 곳의 생산성 증가는 미미한 상태다. 2분기 45.6%의 저축률은 돈이 부족하지 않음을 보여준다. 문제는 그 돈이 어디로 가는가이다. 자본은 연구, 신규 사업, 인적 자본으로 흘러가야 한다. 노동시장과 교육도 근로자들이 수요가 증가하는 영역으로 이동하도록 도와야 한다. 그런데 2024년 직장 기반 직업 훈련은 한국의 훈련 지출의 1.5%에 불과했으며, OECD 평균은 11.7%다. 정부는 4만 달러를 트로피가 아닌 체크포인트로 여겨야 한다. 우선순위는 반도체 이상의 생산성 향상, 효과적인 훈련 확대, 소비를 억누르는 가계 부채 부담 완화여야 한다. 재정 정책은 또한 금리 인상과 충돌하는 방식으로 수요를 자극하는 것을 피해야 한다. 1953년 1인당 소득 67달러에서 4만 달러로 도달한 한국의 여정은 명백한 성공이다. 그러나 소수 산업에 집중된 자본에 크게 의존하고 유리한 평가 효과에 의존하는 경제는 지속적인 안정성을 보장할 수 없다. 구조적 개혁으로 기업 이익의 흐름을 가계에 확대하고, 주력 산업 이상으로 생산성을 높이고, 청년 노동자들과 노동시장의 연결고리를 회복하지 못하면, 4만 달러는 종잇조각 같은 승리로 남을 것이며, 광범위한 번영이 아닌 기업 재무제표상의 최고조를 반영할 뿐이다.

editorials.title: Paper prosperity
editorials.body: Korea nears $40,000 per capita GNI, but growth is uneven, youth struggle for jobs A nation can cross a $40,000 income threshold without a single dollar reaching the average kitchen table. That uncomfortable contradiction now captures the dilemma at the heart of South Korea’s economy. The Bank of Korea on Tuesday projected that per capita gross national income will exceed $40,000 in 2026, assuming exchange rates hold steady and external shocks stay at bay. After 12 years in the $30,000 range since first crossing that threshold in 2014, the country is finally poised to move up. The milestone is meaningful; however, it is an unusually poor measure of how evenly the economy generates and distributes new income. The latest national accounts explain why. Nominal gross domestic product jumped 26.4 percent from a year earlier in the second quarter, its fastest increase since 1979. Real GNI rose 15.6 percent, the strongest annual gain since 1988. Much of that acceleration, however, comes from a semiconductor boom fueled by global AI investment. In the first eight months, semiconductors accounted for 40.6 percent of exports, with shipments surging 169.6 percent from a year earlier. Such concentration matters because national income is an average. It can rise sharply even when the gains are concentrated in a narrow slice of the economy. The exchange rate adds another layer. Per capita GNI is expressed in dollars, so a stronger won can lift the figure even when productive capacity has changed little. The won’s movement from near 1,600 per dollar to the 1,300s has further inflated the dollar-denominated figure. More important is what happens after corporate profits rise. Chipmakers like Samsung Electronics and SK hynix can earn enormous sums without creating a comparable number of domestic jobs. Gross operating surplus, for instance, rose 18.5 percent in the second quarter from the previous quarter, while employee compensation increased just 1.9 percent. Some gains may reach households through wages, bonuses and dividends, but the path is neither immediate nor assured. Young workers have little reason to celebrate the headline figure. Employment among people aged 15 to 29 fell for the 46th consecutive month in August, declining by 143,000 from a year earlier. Among unemployed young people, 52.7 percent reported experiencing burnout, according to a government survey. Equally problematic is productivity. Korea has become exceptionally good at adding capital to its strongest industries, while productivity gains elsewhere remain modest. A savings rate of 45.6 percent in the second quarter shows that money is hardly scarce. The question is where it goes. Capital needs to flow toward research, new businesses and human capital. Labor markets and education also need to help workers move into areas where demand is growing. Yet workplace-based vocational training accounted for only 1.5 percent of Korea’s training expenditure in 2024, compared with an OECD average of 11.7 percent. The government should treat $40,000 as a checkpoint, not a trophy. Its priority should be raising productivity beyond semiconductors, expanding effective training and reducing the household debt burden that suppresses consumption. Fiscal policy should also avoid stimulating demand in ways that run against monetary restraint. Korea’s journey from a meager $67 in per capita income in 1953 to $40,000 is an undisputed triumph. Yet an economy that depends heavily on capital concentrated in a few industries and favorable valuation effects offers no guarantee of lasting stability. Unless structural reforms broaden the flow of corporate gains to households, raise productivity beyond the leading industries and reconnect young workers with the labor market, $40,000 will stand as a paper victory, reflecting a high-water mark on corporate balance sheets rather than broad-based prosperity. editorial.titleTr: Editorial: Abolishing Semi-Linked Proportional Representation Won't Solve the Satellite Party Problem
summaryTr: The People Power Party has proposed abolishing the semi-linked proportional representation system amid controversy over candidate minister Yong Hye-in's concurrent positions.
However, critics argue this is not a fundamental solution to the satellite party problem.
There are suggestions that the People Power Party, the originator of satellite parties, is attempting to evade its own responsibility.
editorial.bodyTr: As criticism mounted over Gender Equality and Family Minister nominee Yong Hye-in's plan to hold both a ministerial position and a proportional representative seat simultaneously, the People Power Party proposed launching discussions on electoral reform to abolish the semi-linked proportional representation system. summary: 스타트업들이 10년간 반복되는 규제 논의로 혁신이 어렵다고 호소했다.
규제 개선 없이는 한국 스타트업의 경쟁력 강화가 불가능하다는 주장이다.
정부와 업계가 실질적 규제 혁신에 나서야 할 시점이라고 지적했다.
editorials.stance: 규제 중심의 정책에서 벗어나 스타트업 혁신을 적극 지원해야 한다
editorials.titleTr: Editorial: Startups Say Repeating Regulatory Complaints for a Decade Won't Drive Innovation
summaryTr: Startups have complained that innovation is difficult due to regulatory discussions that have been repeated over the past decade.
The argument is that it is impossible to strengthen the competitiveness of Korean startups without regulatory improvements.
It was pointed out that it is time for the government and industry to undertake substantive regulatory innovation.
